adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:30 — sql.TablesList now always fails via the stub RunCommands, so every SQL expression (including those in existing alert rules or saved queries built through UnmarshalSQLCommand) is rejected at build time with a misleading "error reading SQL command" BadRequest.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:20 — QueryFramesInto is a stub that always returns "not implemented", so SQLCommand.Execute always fails, and it does so as a result-level error (rsp.Error with a nil return) rather than a hard failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the prior DuckDB-backed implementation with a new `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` `DB` type whose methods are stubs. In particular, `QueryFramesInto(...)` unconditionally returns `errors.New("not implemented")`. `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` was changed to construct `db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()` and always call `db.QueryFramesInto(...)`, so any execution of `SQLCommand.Execute` will now deterministically hit the stub error path and fail. The finding’s note about it being surfaced via `rsp.Error` is consistent with the shown code setting `rsp.Error = err`, though the exact return signature/behavior after that assignment is not fully visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:131 — The error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is returned whether the feature flag is on or off, so it hides the misconfigured gate and gives operators no hint that a feature toggle is involved.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, ReadQuery’s QueryTypeSQL branch calls enableSqlExpressions(h) and returns fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") when it returns false. But enableSqlExpressions is implemented to always return false (it returns false both inside the if and after it), so the error will be returned regardless of whether featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. This makes the feature gate ineffective and the error message doesn’t indicate a feature-flag gating issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:9 — The PR is titled "Advanced SQL Analytics Framework" but actually removes the DuckDB engine and replaces it with an empty stub DB, a functional regression presented as a feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the DuckDB-backed implementation (`github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck`) from both `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` and replaces it with a new `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` `DB` type whose methods (`TablesList`, `RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`) all return `errors.New("not implemented")`. As a result, SQL parsing/execution paths now cannot work: `TablesList()` in `parser.go` now calls `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands(...)` which will always error, and `SQLCommand.Execute` now calls `db.QueryFramesInto(...)` which will always error. Additionally, `enableSqlExpressions` in `pkg/expr/reader.go` returns `false` unconditionally, causing `QueryTypeSQL` to immediately return `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. This is a concrete functional regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:25 — TablesList still builds SQL with fmt.Sprintf and manual single-quote doubling instead of parameter binding, which becomes an injection path as soon as a real DB is wired back behind NewInMemoryDB.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList still constructs a SQL command via `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` after only doing `strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)`. That’s a real, diff-grounded concern about relying on manual escaping/string interpolation instead of parameter binding. However, the diff also shows `NewInMemoryDB()` now returns a stub DB whose `RunCommands` is `not implemented`, so the claimed “injection path as soon as a real DB is wired” is speculative rather than a currently verifiable security defect in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12 — DB.TablesList is dead code that nothing calls, and it duplicates the package-level TablesList in parser.go, which makes it unclear which one is the real entry point.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new method `(*DB).TablesList(rawSQL string)` in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go`, while `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` already defines a package-level `TablesList(rawSQL string)` that is used as the apparent entry point for table extraction. In the shown changes, callers use `NewInMemoryDB()` only for `RunCommands`/`QueryFramesInto` (e.g., `parser.go` calls `duckDB.RunCommands`, and `SQLCommand.Execute` calls `db.QueryFramesInto`), and no code in this diff calls `DB.TablesList`, making it appear unused/duplicative and unclear which API is intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:194 — enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path, so ReadQuery now rejects all SQL expression queries (dashboards, alert rules, /api/ds/query) even when the sqlExpressions flag is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, ReadQuery now gates QueryTypeSQL on enableSqlExpressions(h). The new enableSqlExpressions function returns false on every path: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then `if enabled { return false }` and finally `return false`. Therefore `enabled` is always false and ReadQuery always returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` for SQL queries, even when the feature flag is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:131 — The new rejection is a plain fmt error saying "sqlExpressions is not implemented" instead of a typed errutil/feature-disabled error, so clients get a misleading message with a different error shape.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go under QueryTypeSQL, the new feature gate returns a plain `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` when disabled. The diff does not introduce any typed/structured error (e.g., via `errutil`) for this condition, so this is a concrete, diff-grounded consistency/API-shape concern about how feature-disabled is reported (even if we can’t prove from the diff alone what clients expect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23 — TablesList now calls a stub that always errors, so NewSQLCommand returns a 400 sql-invalid-sql "error reading SQL command" for every valid SQL query and misreports a server-side gap as a client error.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now does `duckDB := NewInMemoryDB()` and then calls `duckDB.RunCommands(...)`. The new pkg/expr/sql/db.go defines `NewInMemoryDB()` returning a `*DB` whose `RunCommands` always returns `errors.New("not implemented")`, so `TablesList` will deterministically fail for any input. The finding’s downstream claim about `NewSQLCommand` returning a specific 400 error can’t be verified from this diff, but the core issue (TablesList now calling a stub that always errors) is directly shown and would break SQL parsing/validation when exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:100 — Execute now calls a QueryFramesInto stub that always returns "not implemented", so every SQL expression node response carries an error instead of frames.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go, Execute now constructs `db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()` and calls `db.QueryFramesInto(...)`. The newly added implementation in pkg/expr/sql/db.go has `QueryFramesInto(...)` hardcoded to `return errors.New("not implemented")`, so Execute will always set an error and never populate frames when this path is reached. This is a behavior regression from the prior `duck.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto(...)` call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:9 — The new exported DB type and NewInMemoryDB add public pkg/expr/sql API made of non-functional stubs, including a DB.TablesList method that duplicates the package-level TablesList.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new exported type `sql.DB` and `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go`, but all its methods are non-functional stubs returning `errors.New("not implemented")`. The new DB is now used by real code paths in this PR: `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` now calls `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands(...)` inside `TablesList`, and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` now calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto(...)`. If those functions are invoked, they will always fail at runtime. The finding’s point about `DB.TablesList` duplicating the package-level `TablesList` is also verifiable from the diff (the method exists and is redundant).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:195 — enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches (and the flag check is inverted), so SQL expressions are always rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, the newly added enableSqlExpressions function always returns false: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false in both the `if enabled { ... }` branch and the final `return false`. As a result, in the QueryTypeSQL case, `if !enabled { return ..., fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }` will always trigger, rejecting SQL expressions even when the flag is enabled (and the flag check is inverted via `!`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:26 — TablesList now calls the stub DB.RunCommands, which always returns "not implemented", so NewSQLCommand (and the ungated UnmarshalSQLCommand path) fails for every SQL query that worked before.
pkg/expr/sql_command.go:100 — SQLCommand.Execute calls the stub DB.QueryFramesInto, which always errors, so every SQL expression execution fails where go-duck used to return results.
pkg/expr/reader.go:195 — h.features is dereferenced with no nil check, so a reader built with nil FeatureToggles now panics on any SQL query; before this change the SQL path never touched features.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new SQL-gating path in `ReadQuery` that calls `enableSqlExpressions(h)`, and that helper unconditionally dereferences `h.features` via `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` with no nil check. The diff alone does not show whether `ExpressionQueryReader.features` can ever be nil (e.g., constructed with nil FeatureToggles), so the claimed panic is plausible but not directly verifiable from this PR. It is, however, a concrete, diff-grounded risk introduced by the change because the SQL path previously did not touch `h.features`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:131 — When the feature flag is off, the error says "sqlExpressions is not implemented" instead of reporting that the feature is disabled, which misleads callers.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/expr/reader.go` under `case QueryTypeSQL`, when `enableSqlExpressions(h)` returns false the code returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. This matches the finding: the error message indicates lack of implementation rather than explicitly stating the feature flag is disabled, which can mislead callers. The diff shows this is an error-message/UX concern rather than a functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:194 — enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches so the feature is dead even with FlagSqlExpressions on, and no test covers flag enabled vs disabled to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() always returns false: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false in both the `if enabled { ... }` branch and the final return. ReadQuery() uses this and immediately errors for QueryTypeSQL when `!enabled`, so SQL expressions are effectively unreachable even if the feature flag were enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:129 — The new feature-flag gate and "not implemented" error path in ReadQuery for QueryTypeSQL ship without any test for the enabled or disabled case.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new branching behavior in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` for `QueryTypeSQL` (calls `enableSqlExpressions(h)` and returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` when disabled), but this PR does not add or modify any test files to cover either the enabled or disabled path. While the diff can’t prove no tests exist elsewhere, it does show no new/updated tests accompanying this new gate/error behavior.

That DB.RunCommands method is a stub that always returns `errors.New("not implemented")`, so TablesList will always error at `ret, err := duckDB.RunCommands(...)`. The diff also removes the prior go-duck dependency that likely provided a working implementation, so this change introduces broken behavior.
